content.text: Substring is missing `requires n.Valid()` (delete has it).

input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "requires",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "substring lacks the precondition `requires n.Valid()`. Its first statement calls split(n, i), which requires n.Valid(); without that precondition the caller cannot establish the Valid() conjuncts (left in Repr, left.Repr < Repr, Repr == {this}, ...). Adding `requires n.Valid()` to substring (as delete already has) fixes the call."}
EOF
sed -i '311s/^/    requires n.Valid()\n/' program.dfy && sed -n 310,313p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
program.dfy now verifies: Dafny reports "21 verified, 0 errors". The command still exits with code 2, but only because of seven pre-existing "deprecated style: a semi-colon is not needed here" warnings, which aren't verification problems. I left those semicolons alone.

**Cause:** `substring` (line 310) had no `requires n.Valid()`. Its first statement, `split(n, i)`, requires `n.Valid()`, so the verifier couldn't prove any of the `Valid()` conditions it reported (`left in Repr`, `left.Repr < Repr`, `Repr == {this}`, and so on) at that call. `delete`, which makes the same `split` calls, already has this precondition.

**Fix:** I added `requires n.Valid()` to `substring`'s contract, just before its existing `requires 0 <= i < j <= |n.Contents|`. That one line is the only change to the program.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before editing, with `spec_element: "requires"` and `proof_obligation: "bridge"`. None of the three categories fits exactly, since there's no loop involved; it's a missing precondition at a call site.
